summary: etl4/vault/vault_io.py (339 lines) implements all 9 public API methods from vault_io_spec.md section 2 -- read_table, write_partition, row_count, list_ym, ym_from_filename, ym_from_date, ym_from_epoch, extract_ym_from_frame, extract_ym_from_path -- plus the 4 module-level constants (SILVER_VAULT_ROOT, MARTS_ROOT, PARTITIONED_TABLES, NON_PARTITIONED_TABLES). All 4 reader-fallback cases work (empty / monolith-only / partitioned-only / mixed-wins), icao24 stays pandas 'string' dtype, pyarrow column pushdown is wired, and the Spark-shard reader extension (globs '<ym_dir>/*.parquet') lets raw_vault_spark.py's partitioned writes load transparently. write_partition is atomic via .part.parquet.<pid>.tmp + os.replace and deterministic (SHA256 identical on repeat writes).

integration_points.reads: <root>/<name>/part.parquet (monolith fallback) and <root>/<name>/ym=YYYY-MM/*.parquet (partitioned); pyarrow footer only for row_count (O(files))
integration_points.writes: <out_dir>/<name>/ym=<ym>/part.parquet atomically; validates ym against YYYY-MM or SYN-<hex>

SYN-<hex> sentinel: write_partition accepts it, read_table/list_ym/extract_ym_from_path handle it, but it is deliberately not valid against pipeline_watermarks.last_ym CHECK regex. If callers write SYN partitions and then try to set a watermark with the same ym, the INSERT will fail -- this is intentional per architecture section 2.3 (synthetic matrix cells do not advance the calendar watermark).
